name: civl
why: A verification language for concurrent programs, an unusual formal tool for checking parallel code exhaustively.

brief.what_it_is: CIVL (Concurrency Intermediate Verification Language) is a verification language and tool for concurrent programs, per the brew description and scout notes. I could not read its documentation, so I cannot confirm its input languages, outputs, or exact workflow. The brew entry installs a single executable named civl.
brief.why_it_exists: Unable to confirm from the README. The scout note describes it as an unusual formal tool for checking parallel code exhaustively.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, I found nothing: the homepage redirected to a Trac wiki that returned HTTP 500 on every attempt, so I have no first-run or configuration details.
brief.standout: Per the scout note, it is a verification language aimed at concurrent programs and checks them exhaustively, which is unusual next to testing tools. I could not verify this against the project's own pages.
brief.caveats: The homepage was effectively unreachable: it redirects to https://vsl.cis.udel.edu/trac/civl/wiki, which returned HTTP 500, and the Trac root also returned HTTP 500. No README, release date, license, or platform information was available. Everything above beyond the brew description and scout note is unverified.
